newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly dip but heavy fuel gains $1.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly dip but heavy fuel gains $1.

text.p: European oil swaps mostly eased lower on Wednesday after overnight losses triggered by bearish U.S. stock figures but heavy fuel bucked the trend and gained $1 a tonne.
Gasoline slipped $2 a tonne early with brokers pegging June around $203 after physical barges traded either side of that level.
July stayed $6 a tonne lower and crack spreads between gasoline and Brent crude were unchanged at $4.10 a barrel for the third quarter and $3.05 for the fourth.
Naphtha slipped $1.50 a tonne to talk $183.50 for June and $184.50 for July.
Brent CFDs and outright prices also slipped.
Monthly CFDs talked 43 cents under the IPE for the balance of June with forward discounts to the IPE as follows: -33 cents (July), -22 cents (3Q97), -13 cents (4Q97), -6 cents (1998).
Weekly levels slipped a cent or two to trade at 43 cents under July for the balance of this week while outright fourth quarter Brent swaps traded between $19.20 and $19.22.
Gas oil crack spreads narrowed about 10 cents with the fourth quarter valued at $4.70 a barrel and the first quarter next year at $$4.60 a barrel.
Despite other losses heavy fuel edged up $1 a tonne on stronger physical barge trade at $84 and $84.50.
June was pegged around $85 and July at $86.
